threads.body:
Assigning `conversation_id` after `invoke_local_agent()` returns is too late for context propagation: the invocation constructor has already built and attached its OTel context, so inference spans created while `wrapped()` executes cannot inherit this ID. Resolve the session ID first and pass it through the handler's `conversation_id=` parameter when creating the invocation; the current tests only inspect the finished parent span and miss this behavior.

This issue also appears on line 602 of the same file.

threads.body:
nit: Could we replace `Any` with the concrete instance types? All three classes define `session_id`, so direct access is safe. Add `Agent`, `Team`, and `Workflow` imports under `TYPE_CHECKING`.

```suggestion
def _resolve_conversation_id(
    instance: Agent | Team | Workflow,
    args: tuple[object, ...],
    kwargs: dict[str, object],
    wrapped: Callable[..., object],
) -> str | None:
    session_id = get_argument("session_id", wrapped, args, kwargs)
    if session_id is None:
        session_id = instance.session_id
    return str(session_id) if session_id is not None else None
```
